title: [Audit] MCP accepts invalid JSON-RPC versions and Remote accepts mismatched response IDs
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/mcp/src/server.rs:119-138](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L119-L138) validates method/id shape but never requires jsonrpc == "2.0" before dispatch/notifications. [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:78-89](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L78-L89) generates a request ID but accepts the reply based only on ok/result/error, without correlation.

## Conditions and impact
Missing/wrong-version request envelopes can invoke tools or change notification state. A faulty/custom endpoint can make Remote attribute an unsolicited or mismatched result to the current call. These are protocol correctness defects, not authorization bypasses. The standard desktop server echoes IDs and Remote now drops its connection after I/O failure, so the fixed automatic-replay scenario must not be used to inflate impact.

## Recommended remediation
Validate JSON-RPC version before any request/notification dispatch. Require exact outstanding response ID in Remote and reject/discard mismatched or malformed responses.

## Suggested regression coverage
Wrong/missing-version mutating requests must return Invalid Request with zero backend calls; malformed initialized notifications must not change state. A mock endpoint returning missing/wrong ID must never be accepted as success.

title: [Audit] PngSuite corpus downloader extracts unauthenticated HTTP content without digest verification
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[xtask/src/main.rs:227](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/xtask/src/main.rs#L227) defines a plain HTTP archive URL. [xtask/src/main.rs:252-258](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/xtask/src/main.rs#L252-L258) downloads with curl -fsSL and immediately runs tar -xzf, without expected digest. Lines 260–262 validate success by counting .png entries only.

## Conditions and impact
A network intermediary controlling the HTTP response for the opt-in cargo xtask corpus --download command can substitute corpus data that is extracted and accepted. This permits test-oracle substitution and extraction disk consumption. No tar directory-escape or code-execution claim is made. The separate Affinity downloader already uses pinned HTTPS sources and digest verification and is not affected by this specific issue.

## Recommended remediation
Pin/verify a reviewed SHA-256 digest before extraction and prefer HTTPS. Bound download/extraction sizes and allow only intended regular corpus entries.

## Suggested regression coverage
A substituted archive containing a .png filename must fail digest verification before extraction. Cover oversized input and unexpected entry types; verify the pinned valid corpus succeeds.

title: [Audit] Track unmaintained rustybuzz and ttf-parser dependencies reported by RustSec
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (maintenance; not a confirmed vulnerability). **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[Cargo.lock:3624-3639](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/Cargo.lock#L3624-L3639) locks rustybuzz 0.20.1; [Cargo.lock:4306-4313](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/Cargo.lock#L4306-L4313) locks ttf-parser 0.25.1. Lockfile dependency edges are krilla 0.8.2 → rustybuzz → ttf-parser. An OSV query of all 564 registry package/version entries returned [RUSTSEC-2026-0206](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0206.html) and [RUSTSEC-2026-0192](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0192.html), both explicitly informational/unmaintained.

## Conditions and impact
These crates remain in the resolved dependency graph but upstream maintainers have stopped fixes. This creates maintenance/security-response risk over time; neither advisory establishes an exploitable defect in these versions. Do not classify these notices as equivalent to the active ruzstd advisory reported separately.

## Recommended remediation
Track a compatible krilla/dependency update that removes the unmaintained chain, or document a reviewed maintenance plan. Advisory-listed alternatives include harfrust for shaping and skrifa for font parsing; avoid swapping algorithms without output validation.

## Suggested regression coverage
After any migration, verify shaping, font subsetting/PDF export, representative scripts and malformed-font handling plus native/WASM builds. Rerun advisory scanning and ensure notices disappear for the intended reason.

title: Native save/reopen changes live warped text inside a symbol
author: excited-raccoon
body:
A symbol containing live point type inside a Wave envelope changes its rendered glyph contours after saving to `.vectorcraft` and reopening in a fresh process. The same envelope outside a symbol round-trips unchanged. This makes a saved editable logo/wordmark look different when reopened.

## Minimal reproduction

Uses the bundled Source Sans 3 font. No rotation, reflection, duplication, cross-document paste or external artwork is needed.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repro_dir="$(mktemp -d -t vectorcraft-symbol-envelope-XXXXXX)"
vectorcraft-cli run \
  --cmd file.new --params '{"width":600,"height":300,"colorMode":"rgb"}' \
  --cmd text.create --params '{"x":30,"y":160,"text":"STUDIO","size":72,"font":"Source Sans 3","color":"#E3AB49"}' \
  --cmd text.fonts \
  --cmd object.envelope.makeWithWarp --params '{"style":"wave","bend":18}' \
  --cmd symbol.new --params '{"name":"Master"}' \
  --cmd document.save --params "{\"path\":\"$repro_dir/document.vectorcraft\"}" \
  --export "$repro_dir/before.png" --scale 2 > "$repro_dir/create.jsonl"
vectorcraft-cli convert "$repro_dir/document.vectorcraft" "$repro_dir/after.png" --scale 2 \
  > "$repro_dir/reopen.jsonl"
printf '%s\n' "$repro_dir"
```

Compare `before.png` with `after.png` in the printed directory. Both are 1200 × 600. The warped letters change contour/position when the native file is reopened; this is visible around the tops and bottoms of the letters.

## Expected

Reopening a native file should retain the same live envelope/symbol appearance. No text, warp parameters, instance transform, font or artboard setting changed.

## Observed and controls

- All commands, save and reopen succeed. Save/export report no warnings.
- `text.fonts` reports Source Sans 3 Regular with `status: exact`, `missing: false`, and zero missing glyphs.

title: Arrow keys don't work in the search / command palette
author: delit
body:
## Summary

The search function (opened from the magnifier icon in the top bar) shows a list of matching commands, but the **arrow keys cannot be used to move through the results**. The list can only be used with the mouse, which breaks the keyboard-only workflow that a command search is meant to support.

## Current behavior

- Open the search from the magnifier icon in the top bar (see screenshot 2).
- Type a query, for example `Artboard`. A list of matching commands appears (see screenshot 1).
- The first result is highlighted (blue), but pressing **Up Arrow** / **Down Arrow** does **not** move the selection to other results.
- The only way to pick another result is to hover or click it with the mouse.

## Expected behavior

| Key | Expected result |
|---|---|
| **Down Arrow** | Move the selection to the next result |
| **Up Arrow** | Move the selection to the previous result |
| **Enter** | Run the selected command |
| **Esc** | Close the search |

Additional details:

- The highlighted result should scroll into view if the list is longer than the visible area.
- Navigation should wrap around (optional): Down on the last result goes to the first, and Up on the first goes to the last.
- Keyboard selection and mouse hover should not conflict. The most recent input (key or mouse) decides which result is highlighted.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Vectorcraft.
2. Click the magnifier icon in the top bar to open the search.
3. Type `Artboard`.
4. Press **Down Arrow** or **Up Arrow**.
5. Observe that the highlighted result does not change.

## Why this matters

- A command search is mainly used from the keyboard. Having to reach for the mouse after typing slows users down.
- Arrow key + Enter navigation is the standard behavior in command palettes and search menus (e.g. VS Code, Illustrator, Figma).
- It is also an accessibility issue for users who cannot or prefer not to use a mouse.

## Suggested solution

- Keep a "selected index" state in the search results list.

title: Allow creating custom standalone (floating) toolbars like Illustrator
author: delit
body:
## Summary

It is currently not possible to create a **custom, standalone toolbar** in Vectorcraft. Users should be able to create one or more new toolbars, pick which tools go into them, and place them freely on the screen (floating or docked). This lets everyone build a compact toolbar with just the tools and shortcuts they use most.

## Current behavior

- Vectorcraft only has the default toolbar.
- There is no way to create a new toolbar, choose which tools it contains, or let it float independently of the main toolbar.
- Users who only need a handful of tools still have to work with the full toolbar or jump between tool groups.

## Expected behavior

Users should be able to:

- [ ] Create a **new toolbar** from a menu (e.g. *New Toolbar...*)
- [ ] Give the toolbar a **name**
- [ ] Choose which **tools and shortcuts** are in it, for example by dragging them from an "All Tools" panel

- [ ] **Rename, edit and delete** toolbars via a *Manage Toolbars...* dialog
- [ ] Have custom toolbars **saved in the workspace** so they come back when switching workspace (see also the workspace issue about remembering panel widths)

## Reference: how Adobe Illustrator does it

Illustrator has a toolbar menu with the options **Advanced**, **Basic**, **Getting Started**, **New Toolbar...** and **Manage Toolbars...**. An "All Tools" panel lists every tool, grouped by category, and tools can be dragged into a new toolbar. The result is a small floating toolbar with only the chosen tools (see screenshots).

## Why this matters

- Users can build a toolbar tailored to their own workflow, for example one for drawing, one for editing paths, one for text.
- Frequently used tools become one click away, without digging through tool groups.

title: Intertwine is missing: make overlapping objects pass over and under each other
author: delit
body:
## Summary

Vectorcraft has no **Intertwine** feature at all. Intertwine lets the user make overlapping objects look woven together, so one object passes *over* another in one overlap area and *under* it in the next, without permanently changing the objects. It is commonly used for interlocking logos, rings, knots, Celtic-style patterns, ribbons and lettering with overlapping strokes.

## Current behavior

- There is no Intertwine command anywhere in the Object menu or the command search.
- The only workaround is to manually duplicate objects, cut them apart, and rearrange the stacking order. This is slow and destructive, and breaks as soon as a shape is edited.

## Expected behavior

A non-destructive Intertwine workflow, following Illustrator's `Object > Intertwine`:

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Make** | Turns the selected overlapping objects into an *Intertwine group* (shown as a group in the Layers panel). Additional objects can be dragged into the group later. |
| **Edit** | Re-enters the Intertwine group so the intertwined areas can be changed. |
| **Release** | Restores the objects to their original state and removes the Intertwine group. |

Choosing the overlap areas:

- [ ] **Hover/click** an overlapping area to intertwine it
- [ ] **Draw an enclosed path** around an overlapping area (or around an area where three or more objects overlap) to intertwine it
- [ ] The path of the object nearest to the pointer is **highlighted** while hovering, so it is clear which object will go on top

Supported objects:

- [ ] Shapes and paths
- [ ] Text
- [ ] Ideally 2D and 3D objects, if Vectorcraft supports them

Limitations (same as Illustrator, acceptable for a first version):

- Nested Intertwine groups are not supported
- Objects already inside an Intertwine group cannot be used to create a new one
- Not supported together with Live Paint, Repeat or graphs

## Reference

Adobe documentation: [Intertwine objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/inter…

title: Two geometry tests fail on macOS x86_64 (pass on FreeBSD CI)
author: ham9zah
body:
Two geometry tests fail on `main` (0d0ea352) on my macOS x86_64 machine: one in `vectorcraft-engine` and one in `vectorcraft-pathops`. The FreeBSD CI job passes on the same commit, and no CI job runs the tests on macOS, so this may be a platform difference (floating-point details) rather than a bug in `main`. I only ran them on this one machine.

## 1. `tests_build::shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly`

In `crates/engine/src/tests_build.rs` (see #569).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft
cd vectorcraft
git checkout 0d0ea352
cargo test -p vectorcraft-engine --lib shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly
```

```
thread 'tests_build::shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly' panicked at crates/engine/src/tests_build.rs:1110:13:
NodeId(65) has an outline 0.778 pt wide on average, 102.8 pt long
```

This is the "no outline is a sliver or carries a spur" check: one outline of the selection is 0.778 pt wide on average, the test wants more than 1.0 pt. It fails the same way at 504e7192, where I first saw it.

## 2. `every_pathfinder_operation_is_pinned`

In `crates/pathops/tests/pathfinder_pinned.rs`.

```sh
git checkout 0d0ea352
cargo test -p vectorcraft-pathops --test pathfinder_pinned
```

```
thread 'every_pathfinder_operation_is_pinned' panicked at crates/pathops/tests/pathfinder_pinned.rs:49:5:
assertion `left == right` failed
```

One of the 40 pinned hashes differs: entry 10 (0-based; the Unite of the 5 shapes, seed 7). It is computed here as `60181664961792917`, the pinned value is `9388160212451732406`; the other 39 match. Both tests fail every time, alone and in `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (6070 pass, these two fail; that run was without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`).

title: AI import: global process CMYK swatch read as spot with wrong values; PDF export renders it near-black
author: drumanshoo
body:
## Summary
Opening an Illustrator `.ai` file, a global **process** CMYK swatch is imported as a **spot** colour with the wrong CMYK values. Exporting to PDF then writes a `/Separation` whose alternate colour is that wrong value, so the swatch renders near-black in any PDF viewer. PNG and SVG exports of the same file look correct, so the problem is easy to miss.

## Version / platform
VectorCraft 0.10.0 (`vectorcraft-cli 0.10.0`), Windows 11 x64, portable build.

## What happens
The source file is a client logo saved by Illustrator (PDF-compatible `.ai`, PDF 1.6). I can't post it publicly. Its XMP swatch metadata defines the swatch as:

```xml
<xmpG:swatchName>PMS3538 CP C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0</xmpG:swatchName>
<xmpG:type>PROCESS</xmpG:type>
<xmpG:mode>CMYK</xmpG:mode>
<xmpG:cyan>93.000001</xmpG:cyan>
<xmpG:magenta>10.000000</xmpG:magenta>
<xmpG:yellow>0.000000</xmpG:yellow>
<xmpG:black>0.000000</xmpG:black>
```

`vectorcraft-cli run --in logo.ai --cmd swatch.list` reports:

```json
{"name": "PMS3538 CP C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0", "spot": true, "global": true,
 "color": {"model": "cmyk", "c": 1.0, "m": 1.0, "y": 0.0, "k": 0.93}, "hex": "#171426"}
```

So it is marked `spot: true` (the source says PROCESS), and the values look shuffled or clamped (expected c=0.93 m=0.10 y=0 k=0).

`vectorcraft-cli convert logo.ai logo.pdf` then writes:

```
/Separation/PMS3538#20CP#20C=93#20M=10#20Y=0#20K=0/DeviceCMYK<</FunctionType 2/Domain[0 1]/Range[0 1 0 1 0 1 0 1]/C0[0 0 0 0]/C1[1 1 0 0.92941177]/N 1>>
```

Poppler (`pdftoppm`) and PdfCraft both render that area as about `#03030c` / `#000017` (near-black) where the logo is cyan. `convert logo.ai logo.png` and `logo.svg` render the cyan correctly (about `#009be5`).

## Expected
The swatch is imported as a process colour, C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0, and the PDF renders it cyan.

## Notes

title: [Feature Request] [VectorCraft] Contextual Skew / Shear Cursor on Bounding Box Hover (Quality of Life)
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Currently, performing a simple tilt or shear (inclination) on an object requires switching to a dedicated transformation tool or manually entering values in a transform panel. 

I propose adding a direct canvas shear gesture using the default Selection Tool, similar to the behavior in Affinity Designer. This allows users to skew objects dynamically without interrupting their workflow to switch tools.

Proposed Behavior & Interaction:

1. Activation:
   - Select any object using the standard Selection Tool.
   - Position the mouse pointer slightly outside the bounding box edge (between two edge/corner handles).

2. Cursor Change:
   - The cursor dynamically changes into a two-way opposing arrows icon (up/down arrows for vertical edges, or left/right arrows for horizontal edges), signaling that a shear action is available.

3. Execution:
   - Click and drag along the edge:
     * Dragging up/down along a vertical edge skews the object vertically.
     * Dragging left/right along a horizontal edge skews the object horizontally.

Key Benefits:
- Time-saving: Eliminates constant tool-switching or panel navigation for minor text/shape tilt adjustments.
- Intuitive UX: Follows well-established vector editing standards, making canvas interactions smoother and more fluid.

title: Fonts: a classic Mac TrueType whose cmap has no Unicode subtable is listed, but every character is missing (and an ideographic space sets at zero width)
author: imachus
body:
### What happens

Some classic Mac TrueType fonts (suitcase files: an empty data fork, the `sfnt` in the resource fork) carry only Macintosh cmap subtables: `(1, 0)` format 0 and `(1, 1)` format 2 (Mac Japanese, i.e. Shift-JIS). I have several of these in a font folder (old DynaFont and Ricoh HG families, sold that way in the 2000s). The scan reads them and lists them in the font menus by their names — but no character maps:

- `text.fonts` reports every character as missing: on a newsletter of 348 distinct characters set in one of them, `missingGlyphs` is 347 (the one exception is U+3000, see below). Kana, kanji, and in these fonts even ASCII digits and letters.
- The type still draws, because each missing glyph is drawn in the fallback font — so the font looks as if it worked, only in the wrong face.
- An ideographic space (U+3000) is the exception: whitespace counts as covered by the primary font (`crates/text/src/shape.rs`, `let covered = c.is_whitespace() || …`), so it isn't sent to the fallback. It's laid out with glyph 0's advance, which is 0 in these fonts, and paragraph indents vanish. For comparison, in Times New Roman, which also lacks U+3000, `あ　あ` measures 3 em; in one of these fonts it measures 2 em.

### Why

`skrifa`'s `Charmap` picks a Unicode subtable, else the Windows symbol one, else Mac Roman `(1, 0)`. With no Unicode subtable, every lookup goes through the Mac Roman table, which in these fonts maps (almost) nothing. The Mac Japanese subtable (format 2) is never read, and reading it would need a Shift-JIS → Unicode table, which the crate doesn't have.

### To reproduce without these fonts

Take any TrueType the tests use, drop every cmap subtable except a `(1, 0)` format 0 one (or keep only a `(1, 1)` format 2 one), wrap it in a resource fork with `suitcase::fork_of` and put it in a scanned folder as a suitcase (empty data fork). It's listed by name; `text.create` with it gives `missingGlyphs` = every non-space character; `あ　あ` measures 2 em ins…

title: [Feature] Stroke Width tool like Affinity's: on-canvas width profile editing, locks, snapping and a profile chart

### Description

Improve the **Width tool** so that it edits a stroke's width profile on the canvas, as Affinity's **Stroke Width Tool** does (public documentation: https://www.affinity.studio/help/tools-tools-stroke-width/ and https://affinity.help/designer2/en-US.lproj/pages/Tools/tools_lineWidth.html, https://affinity.help/designer2/en-US.lproj/pages/CurvesShapes/edit_pressureProfiles.html).

The goal: draw a stroke with the Pencil, the Pen or a brush, then shape its width directly on the curve, with exact control, snapping and an editable profile chart that stays in step with the canvas.

### What VectorCraft has today

- **Width profile presets** in the Stroke panel.

**1. Editing on the canvas**
- Click on a stroke to **add a width point**. Drag a point's handle inward or outward to change the width there. Drag the point along the curve to move it.
- **Modifier drag to lock the position:** change only the width at that point.
- **Modifier drag to lock the width:** move the point along the curve and keep its width.
- **Modifier-click a point:** opens a dialog to type an exact width at that point (the existing Width Point Edit dialog can serve).
- **Double-click a point or its handle:** deletes the point.
- Handles are **symmetric** by default. **One-sided widths** on a closed curve: a modifier drag at the start/end point unlinks the two sides. **Double-click a start/end handle** makes the two widths equal (the smaller takes the larger).
- Works on strokes from the **Pencil**, the **Pen** and the **brushes**.

title: Allow Ctrl/Cmd and Alt modifier chords for tool shortcuts
author: earlvanze
body:
## Summary

The Keyboard Shortcuts editor currently permits tool bindings only as a single key, optionally with Shift. Command shortcuts accept Ctrl/Cmd and Alt modifiers, but tools cannot use those chords.

## Requested behavior

Allow tool shortcuts to use the same supported modifier chords as command shortcuts, with conflict detection and platform-appropriate Ctrl/Cmd display.

## Current behavior

Attempting to assign a tool shortcut with Ctrl/Cmd or Alt is rejected by the editor. The relevant source validation reports that tool shortcuts must be a single key, optionally with Shift.

## Scope

This is distinct from #487, which fixed recording modified command chords.

## Reporter context

A community report requested more flexible custom tool bindings. No OS or build was supplied.

title: G16: complete Brazilian Portuguese (pt-br) interface
author: Messhias
body:
## Context

Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-br`) already ships as a **partial** catalog: every menu label and every `tl!` literal that were current when it was written, plus many `@msg` rows from later follow-ups (#384, #1205). It is still at ~68% in [localization-parity.md](docs/localization-parity.md): `complete_menus` is false, it is not in `COMPLETE_MESSAGES`, and strings added since the catalog was last filled fall back to English.

This is part of **G16 Localization** in [docs/gaps.md](docs/gaps.md) (the twelve key languages). Completing `pt-br` does not close G16 (Hindi, Arabic and Indonesian remain), but it finishes one of the key Latin-script languages that is only partial today.

## Proposal

Bring `pt-br` to the same bar as Spanish / French / Vietnamese:

1. Translate every current menu string and `tl!` literal still missing from `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/pt-br.tsv` (clean-room, from the English meaning, ordinary Brazilian Portuguese computing / vector vocabulary already used in the catalog).
2. Translate every status / error message the `COMPLETE_MESSAGES` scan requires (`@msg` rows).
3. Set `complete_menus: true` on the `pt-br` `LangInfo` and add `pt-br` to `COMPLETE_MESSAGES` so the existing tests keep it complete.
4. Update progress docs (`ROADMAP.md`, `docs/localization-parity.md`, `docs/gaps.md`, `docs/target-app-parity.md`, `docs/development.md` as needed).

Leave in English on purpose (`MENU_KEEP_AS_IS`): product name, language names, OpenType, built-in workspace names, bracketed perspective grid preset names. Product and technology names (VectorCraft, SVG, CMYK, …) stay in Latin letters.

## Out of scope

- Locale-aware number/date formats
- Help content
- Inventing UI strings that are not in the English source / dump

## Assignee

@Messhias (native Brazilian Portuguese speaker) — working on a branch for this.

title: Dimension tool: edit the dimension text (text override with <> for the measured value)
author: lewandowskit
body:
Follow-up idea for the Dimension tool (#1372, #1788).

**What:** let people type what a dimension shows instead of its measured value: double-click a dimension (or Object › Dimensions › Edit Dimension Text…) and enter text, with `<>` standing for the measurement, e.g. `<> ±0.5`, `ok. <>`, or plain `1200 mm`. An empty field shows the measurement again. The measurement itself keeps following the measured art, so `<>` stays live.

**Why:** we prepare sign, banner and Dibond jobs, and my wife dimensions customer drawings very often. Drawings are often not to scale (a sketch of a 6 m façade sign on an A4 sheet), or need a tolerance, a note or a rounded value for the customer. Today, once a dimension is placed, its number can't be changed: the only option is to ungroup it and lose the link.

**Prior art:** CAD tools and CorelDRAW have this as a "text override" of a dimension. I know this is not part of Illustrator's documented Dimension tool, so it's the owner's call — hence an issue rather than a change inside #1788.

**Ready implementation:** I've built it on top of #1788, with tests, if it's wanted: https://github.com/lewandowskit/vectorcraft/commits/wymiary-tekst

- `Dimension.text` (stored only when set) with `measured_label()`; `label()` applies the text.
- `dimension.create` / `dimension.update` take `text` (string; `""`/null = the measurement), one line of at most 256 characters.
- An Edit Dimension Text dialog (measured value, text field, live preview, Use Measured Value), opened by double-clicking a dimension with the selection tools or the Dimension tool, and the UI command `dimension.editText {id?}`.
- Strings in every catalog; engine and dialog tests (live `<>`, undo, save/open, reset, invalid text).

It can be rebased onto whatever #1788 becomes once the documented gesture and Properties-panel work lands — or the text field could live in that Properties section instead of a dialog.

title: Plug-in runs fail with "instruction budget" at random when memory.copy/memory.fill crosses the 20M fuel slice; and a request for a larger plug-in budget
author: natdesigntak
body:
**Version:** VectorCraft 0.10.0 (macOS, Apple Silicon); source checked at 0d0ea35.

### 1. Bug: a bulk memory instruction at a fuel-slice boundary ends the run

`crates/plugins/src/runtime.rs` `call()` gives a plug-in its fuel in slices of `FUEL_SLICE` (20,000,000) and resumes on `TypedResumableCall::OutOfFuel`. That works for ordinary instructions. But when the instruction that runs out of fuel is a bulk `memory.copy` or `memory.fill` (rustc emits these for `copy_from_slice`, `vec![0; n]` and so on), wasmi does not return a resumable `OutOfFuel`. It returns an `Err` with trap code `OutOfFuel` from `call_resumable` / `resume`. `wasm_err` turns that into `Error::Limit("instruction budget")`, so the run fails even though most of the budget is unused.

Which runs fail depends on where the 20M boundaries fall, so the same plug-in on the same input can pass or fail after a small change to the input.

**Repro:** any filter that does a large `memory.fill` or `memory.copy` and runs a bit over 20M instructions. Our nesting plug-in hit it on larger jobs (well over 20M instructions). Building the same code with binaryen's `wasm-opt --llvm-memory-copy-fill-lowering` (which turns the bulk ops into loops) makes the failures go away, and the run uses the same budget.

**Possible fixes:** when an `Err` carries `TrapCode::OutOfFuel` and `left > 0`, top up the fuel and retry, if wasmi allows the bulk op to be re-run after a top-up (we have not checked this in wasmi's source). Or give the whole budget in one go when no deadline is needed. Or, at minimum, say "plug-in hit a fuel slice" rather than "instruction budget" so authors know what happened.

### 2. Request: a larger or configurable budget for object filters

An object filter gets `50,000,000 + 4,000 × input bytes` instructions (`Limits::default()`), and users cannot change this. That is fine for recolouring or path clean-up. It is too small for heavier filters such as nesting, which packs parts onto sheets for CNC and laser cut…

title: A string for an optional number parameter is silently ignored ("60 mm")
author: nes-cape
body:
## What happens

A string for an optional number parameter is silently ignored. `object.setBounds {"width":"60 mm"}` returns `{"ids":[2]}`, exits 0 and leaves the object at its old width. A string for a required number (`shape.rectangle {"x":"abc"}`) is an error, so only optional parameters are affected.

## Expected

An error that the value is not a number (or the unit string is parsed).

## Steps to reproduce

1. `vectorcraft-cli run --cmd file.new --params '{"width":300,"height":200}' --cmd shape.rectangle --params '{"x":10,"y":10,"width":50,"height":40}' --cmd object.setBounds --params '{"width":"60 mm"}' --cmd document.inspect`
2. Exit status is 0; `document.inspect` still shows width 50 and the history has no transform step.

## Version

VectorCraft 0.10.0, CLI, macOS universal, macOS 26.1 (25B78)

title: PDF/X-4 embeds a loaded ICC profile twice; output.profiles none has no effect
author: nes-cape
body:
## What happens

A PDF/X-4 export with a loaded ICC profile embeds that profile twice: two identical ICC streams (2,195,228 bytes each for PSO Coated v3), one as the output intent's DestOutputProfile and one as the ICCBased colour space of the fills. A one-rectangle document is 3.5 MB; the same export with the built-in profile is about 250 kB. `output.profiles: "none"` makes no difference: both streams are still there.

## Expected

The profile is embedded once and referenced from both places, as InDesign and Acrobat do, and `output.profiles: "none"` leaves the colours untagged as the parameter description says.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `vectorcraft-cli run --cmd color.loadProfile --params '{"path":"/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/PSOcoated_v3.icc"}' --cmd file.new --params '{"colorMode":"cmyk"}' --cmd shape.rectangle --params '{"x":10,"y":10,"width":100,"height":50,"fill":"#504b44"}' --cmd edit.colorSettings --params '{"cmyk":"PSO Coated v3"}' --cmd document.exportPdf --params '{"path":"a.pdf","standard":"pdfX4","output":{"outputIntent":"PSO Coated v3"}}'`
2. The same with `"output":{"profiles":"none","outputIntent":"PSO Coated v3"}` as b.pdf.
3. Inflate the streams of both files: two streams starting with an ICC header (`acsp` at offset 36), identical length; a.pdf and b.pdf are both 3.5 MB.

## Version

VectorCraft 0.10.0, CLI, macOS universal, macOS 26.1 (25B78)

title: color.loadProfile registers a profile for the current run only
author: nes-cape
body:
## What happens

A profile registered with `color.loadProfile` is only known inside the `run` that loaded it. In the next `run`, `edit.colorSettings {"cmyk": "PSO Coated v3"}` does not find it and the working CMYK stays on the built-in profile. The description of `color.loadProfile` says "register an ICC profile (native only)" and does not mention that it is per run.

## Expected

Either the profile stays registered across runs (like a profile in ~/Library/ColorSync/Profiles), or the description says the registration lasts for one run only.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `vectorcraft-cli run --cmd color.loadProfile --params '{"path":"/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/PSOcoated_v3.icc"}'` (any CMYK ICC file; the result names the profile).
2. `vectorcraft-cli run --cmd file.new --params '{"colorMode":"cmyk"}' --cmd edit.colorSettings --params '{"cmyk":"PSO Coated v3"}' --cmd document.exportPdf --params '{"path":"a.pdf","standard":"pdfX4","output":{"outputIntent":"PSO Coated v3"}}'`
3. The PDF's output intent is still the built-in "VectorCraft Generic CMYK (SWOP-like)". Loading the profile again in step 2's run gives FOGRA51 / PSO Coated v3.

## Version

VectorCraft 0.10.0, CLI, macOS universal, macOS 26.1 (25B78)

title: Feature request: Super Marquee-style selection tool (never moves objects, Enclosing / Touch modes)
author: cairodavila
body:
### What I'd like

A marquee tool that only selects, like Astute Graphics' Super Marquee (the ColliderScribe plug-in for Illustrator): https://docs.astutegraphics.com/colliderscribe/super-marquee-tool/super-marquee-tool-operations

Press-drag always draws a marquee, even if you start on top of an object, and never moves anything, like the Lasso. It has two modes:

- **Enclosing:** only objects fully inside the marquee get selected.
- **Touch** (they call it Traditional): anything the marquee touches, which is what the Selection tool does today.

`E` switches between them while dragging. The marquee is dashed in Enclosing and solid in Touch, so you can tell which one you're in. Shift adds, Alt subtracts, and it selects whole objects only.

### Why

With the Selection tool, a drag that starts over an object moves it. To marquee something sitting on a background I have to lock the background, select, then unlock it again. Enclosing mode is where it hurts most, because you only get to it after the drag has started, so you can't start from over any art.

I know this isn't Illustrator parity. In #927 I read that ideas beyond Illustrator are decided case by case, so I'm opening this to ask, not assuming.

### Alternatives considered

A smaller version: no new tool, just a modifier on the Selection tool that makes a drag over an object draw a marquee instead of moving it, plus `E` for Enclosing from the start of the drag.

Super Marquee has a lot more (highlighting what's about to be selected, other marquee shapes, Boolean mode, alternating and random selection). Highlighting would be the nicest follow-up, I don't need the rest.

### Additional context

Related but different: #1103 made marquees select only what they touch. Tested on VectorCraft 0.10.0.

title: Direct Selection: double-clicking type should switch to the Type tool (parity with #284)
author: el-j
body:
### Expected behavior
In #284, double-clicking type with the Selection tool (`v`) was implemented to switch to the Type tool and position the caret at the clicked character for immediate inline editing.
The Direct Selection tool ("white arrow", shortcut `a`) should behave the same way: double-clicking a text element (standalone or nested inside a group) should switch directly to the Type tool and position the caret at the clicked character, without requiring the user to switch tools manually.

### Current behavior
Double-clicking a text object with the Direct Selection tool only checked for live corner widgets (`corners::double_click`) and ignored text objects, requiring users to manually select the Type tool (`t`) before they could edit text.

### Proposed fix
In `DirectSelectionTool::pointer` under `(PointerKind::DoubleClick, _) if !self.group`, hit-test for text nodes (`NodeKind::Text`) at the click point (inspecting leaf objects so nested text in groups is directly reachable) and emit `Action::SwitchTool("type".into())`.

title: Type tool: Escape should return to the selection tool used before double-clicking, preserving group isolation
author: el-j
body:
### Expected behavior
1. When double-clicking into text editing using a selection tool (such as the Direct Selection tool or Selection tool), pressing `Escape` should end text editing and return back to the tool that was used before double-clicking into text.
2. When the user drills into a group using the Selection tool (entering isolation mode) and double-clicks a text element to edit it, pressing `Escape` the first time should end text editing and switch back to the Selection tool while *preserving* isolation mode. A second `Escape` press should then be required to exit isolation mode.

### Current behavior
1. `TypeTool::key(ToolKey::Escape)` always hardcodes switching to `"selection"` (`Action::SwitchTool("selection".into())`), so if the user double-clicked text while using the Direct Selection tool (`"directSelection"`), `Escape` unexpectedly switches them to the standard Selection tool (`"selection"`).
2. If `Escape` is claimed during text editing in isolation mode, `Escape` wasn't explicitly consumed in egui shortcuts, risking inconsistent isolation exit behavior on the same press.

### Proposed fix
1. Track the originating tool in `TypeTool` (`prevTool`) when double-clicking into type from canvas.
2. On `ToolKey::Escape`, return `Action::SwitchTool(self.prev_tool.take().unwrap_or_else(|| "selection".into()))`.
3. In `shortcuts::handle`, consume `Key::Escape` when claimed by the active tool so that the first `Escape` ends text editing without triggering `object.exitIsolation`. A second `Escape` press (when no longer editing text) then exits isolation mode.

title: [Tools] v0.11.0: Eraser creates jagged/dense anchor points; Simplify Path is overly aggressive at 1pt
author: wcosta09
body:
### Environment
- App Version: VectorCraft v0.11.0
- OS: Windows 11

### Bug Description
Two interrelated vector path calculation issues:
1. **Eraser Tool generates excessive anchors:** Slicing through or erasing vector shapes creates an excessive amount of redundant, jagged anchor points along the cut edge, resulting in wavy, deformed silhouettes rather than clean Bézier curves.
2. **Simplify Path is overly aggressive:** Attempting to clean up these points using the Simplify feature destroys the shape geometry even at the lowest setting. Setting tolerance to 1pt reduced a path from 205 anchor points down to 11 points, flattening out curves and completely distorting the object's original silhouette.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In VectorCraft v0.11.0, create a vector shape.
2. Use the Eraser tool to erase a section of the shape.
3. Observe the dense cluster of redundant points created along the cut.
4. Select the path and apply 'Object > Path > Simplify' with tolerance set to 1pt.

### Expected Behavior
- The Eraser tool should apply an automated curve-fitting pass with optimal Bézier anchor distribution.
- The Simplify command should provide subtle, progressive point reduction without abruptly collapsing the geometry at low tolerance values (like 1pt).

title: .ai import: a layer's own opacity in the editing data is dropped
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**VectorCraft 0.11.0** (macOS universal).

A layer given an opacity of its own (targeted in the Layers panel, then Transparency) is written in the .ai's editing data after the layer's art, just before `LB`. Illustrator 30.6 saves a layer at 35% as:

```
...
f
...
0 0.35 0 2 0 Xy
0 0 Xd
7 () XW
LB
```

A group at 35% gets the same two lines after its `U`, with `6 () XW`. VectorCraft draws the group at its opacity, but the layer at full opacity. That shows two ways:
- **The layers go.** When the layer covers enough of the page, the check against the PDF part, which draws the layer at 35%, rejects the editing data ("the file's layers weren't read from its editing data (the art on them differs from the page's in N% of it)"), and every sublayer is lost.
- **The art is too dark.** Otherwise, or with `editingData: "always"` (`convert --editing-data`), the layer's art draws opaque.

In `crates/eps/src/import/ai/read.rs` (v0.11.0), `transparency()` (line 1389) sets the opacity and blend on the last object only when that is a group or compound path. Before `LB` the last object is the layer's last path, and `end_layer()` (line 854) builds the layer node without an opacity or blend. So a blend mode set on a layer is presumably lost the same way; I haven't made a file for that.

**Repro.** `make_layer_opacity.py` (below) replaces ROOF's outline in #1025's `A-control.txt` with a black square. It gives ROOF an opacity of 35%, in the editing data as Illustrator 30.6 writes it and in the PDF part as `/ca 0.35`, and wraps it as #1025's `wrap_ai.py` does. `group-opacity.ai` is the control: the same square in a group at 35%, the layer at 100%.

```

vectorcraft-cli info layer-opacity.ai
vectorcraft-cli convert layer-opacity.ai layer.png --scale 2 --editing-data
vectorcraft-cli info group-opacity.ai
vectorcraft-cli convert group-opacity.ai group.png --scale 2 --editing-data

title: .ai import: an opacity mask in the editing data is ignored, so the masked art draws whole
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**VectorCraft 0.11.0** (macOS universal).

Illustrator 30.6 writes an opacity mask on a layer inside the layer's art dictionary, with the mask's art on `%_` lines between `X=` and `X+`:

```
(ROOF) Ln
1 AE
%_/ArtDictionary :
%_/XMLUID : (ROOF) ; (AI10_ArtUID) ,
%_/Mask :
%_1 /Bool (Linked) ,
%_0 /Bool (Disabled) ,
%_X=
%_... the mask's art ...
%_X+
%_ (Art) ,
%_1 /Bool (Clipping) ,
%_0 /Bool (Inverted) ,
%_; (AI9_Mask) ,
%_;
```

VectorCraft reads the layer and its art but not the mask: the art draws in full, with no warning that a mask was left out. Nothing in `crates/eps/src/import/ai/` reads `/Mask` or `AI9_Mask`: at v0.11.0, `git grep -n -i mask -- crates/eps/src/import/ai` finds a lexer comment (`lex.rs:336`), a comment on `Lb`'s operands (`read.rs:1307`), and `read.rs:1248`, which gives new ids to a mask a node already has. That shows two ways:
- **The layers go.** The PDF part draws the art through the mask (an `/SMask`), so where the mask hides enough, the check against it rejects the editing data and every sublayer is lost.
- **Hidden art shows.** With `editingData: "always"` (`convert --editing-data`), or when the masked area is small, what the mask hides is drawn.

**Repro.** `make_layer_mask.py` (below) replaces ROOF's outline in #1025's `A-control.txt` with a black square. It wraps the file as #1025's `wrap_ai.py` does.

title: PDF/.ai import: a document with one image over 256 MB decoded is refused whole (0.10.0 opened it)
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**VectorCraft 0.11.0** (macOS universal).

Since the stream budgets for #1700 and #1701 (991ce2c6, "Importers: PDF streams the reader would fail on are refused"), a PDF or .ai holding one image stream that decodes to more than 256 MB doesn't open at all:

```
cannot read PDF: a stream in it would decode to more than 256 MB, or its decode parameters can't be applied
```

That size is ordinary in print work: an A0 sheet scanned at 300 ppi in RGB is 9930 × 14040 px, 418 MB decoded. An .ai of ours with one such image, 20 MB on disk, opened in 0.10.0 (its 9 layers, from the PDF part), and 0.11.0 refuses it.

**Repro.** `make_big_image.py` (below) writes two one-page PDFs, each holding one flat RGB image:
- `big-image.pdf`: 9930 × 14040 px, 418 MB decoded, 0.4 MB on disk.
- `under-cap.pdf`: 9000 × 9900 px, 267 MB decoded, just under 256 MiB.

```
python3 make_big_image.py
vectorcraft-cli info big-image.pdf
vectorcraft-cli info under-cap.pdf
```

`big-image.pdf` fails with the error above, and `under-cap.pdf` opens.

- **Expected:** the document opens. An image's decoded size is known before decoding (Width × Height × components × bits), so an image over the budget could come in at a reduced resolution, or as a placeholder with a warning, rather than the whole document being refused.
- **In the code:** `MAX_DECODED = 256 << 20` in `crates/pdf/src/streams.rs:15` (v0.11.0) applies to every stream, images included; the message is `STREAM_NOTE` in `crates/pdf/src/pages.rs:118`.

title: [Feature Request] [Bug] Under Wayland on Linux. Pen pressure doesn't work
author: KazuInu
body:
### Description
Under Linux, running a Wayland session. The pen pressure, and generally pen inputs. Don't register under VectorCraft. You can move the pointer, but the UI doesn't react. This is the [Bug] part of this issue.

### Solution
This is the [Feature Request] part of the issue. Just like PhotoCraft. If you run the app under xWayland. Most problems are solved. VectorCraft needs a toggle to start the app under X11. If you start the app with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY [path_to_you_appimage]`. The pen inputs work without problem (exactly like PhotoCraft).
Also. I'm guessing this is going to be a more general problem with the entire ArtCraft apps collection.

### Test environment
- Fedora Linux 44 - KDE Edition
- VectorCraft 0.11.0
- Input: Wacom ONE + Mouse

title: EPS import: Illustrator layers dropped for "Large Canvas" files (%AI24_LargeCanvasScale not applied)
author: CouchRiv
body:
**Component:** EPS import (`crates/eps/src/import/native.rs`, `crates/eps/src/import/ai/`)
**Severity:** High. Every Illustrator EPS made on a Large Canvas document opens flattened into one layer.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| VectorCraft | 0.10.0, `vectorcraft.exe` built 2026-10-12, Windows 11 x64 |
| UI language | French |
| Source files | Adobe Illustrator 30.8.2 (2026), saved as EPS |
| EPS flavour | DOS binary EPS (`C5 D0 D3 C6` header), TIFF preview, no WMF preview, PostScript Level 2, CMYK |
| Editing data | `%AI9_PrivateDataBegin` > `%AI24_DataStream` (ASCII85 + Zstandard), `%AI5_FileFormat 14.0` |

## Summary

Illustrator writes the native editing data of a Large Canvas document at 1/10 scale and declares it with `%AI24_LargeCanvasScale: 10`. VectorCraft decodes the editing data and reads the layers, but does not apply this factor. The native bounding box is then 10x smaller than the PostScript page, the page-match check fails, and the import falls back to "the page, in one layer". All layer names, order, visibility, empty layers and hidden-layer content are lost.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Illustrator 2026, open any Large Canvas document (an artboard wider than 227 in switches Illustrator to Large Canvas, 1:10).
2. Create at least 2 named layers with some art; hide one of them.
3. Save As > Illustrator EPS (TIFF preview, default options).
4. Open the EPS in VectorCraft 0.10.0 (File > Open).

> Steps 1 to 3 are the expected way to produce such a file; we have not run them. We reproduced the bug with 4 real production files (data below). We did not build a minimal file. The production files are client work and cannot be attached publicly. They can be shared privately on request.

## Expected

The layers from the editing data, as in Illustrator: same names, order and visibility, empty layers kept, hidden-layer content kept, at the page's size.

## Actual

- The Layers panel shows one layer, `Layer 1`, rebuilt from the PostScript page.
- Status bar (Fr…

title: EPS import: the fallback discards the Illustrator layer tree even when it was read correctly
author: CouchRiv
body:
Found with the same 4 Illustrator Large Canvas EPS samples as #2031 (environment, samples and layer inventory there). VectorCraft 0.10.0, Windows 11 x64, French UI.

When the native art is rejected, names, order, visibility and empty layers are discarded too, even though the layer tree was read correctly.

title: French UI: EPS import note and generated layer/object names are not translated
author: CouchRiv
body:
Found with the same 4 Illustrator Large Canvas EPS samples as #2031 (environment, samples and layer inventory there). VectorCraft 0.10.0, Windows 11 x64, French UI.

**Severity:** Medium

## Actual
- The whole import note shows in English:
  > Ouvert avec 1 remarque(s) : the file's layers weren't read (its editing data is for a different page): it comes in as its page, in one layer
- The inner fragment `its editing data is for a different page` has a French entry in the `@msg` catalogue ("ses données…"), but the wrapper `the file's layers weren't read ({why}): it comes in as its page, in one layer` has none, so the composed message falls back to English.
- Mixed object names in the Layers panel: `<Tracé>` (translated) next to `<Clip Group>` (untranslated); the generated layer name is `Layer 1` instead of `Calque 1`.

## Expected
Add the wrapper and its variants to the catalogue. Localise generated object and layer names.

title: EPS import: very large Illustrator editing data hits a hard decompression limit (stream it)
author: CouchRiv
body:
Found with the same 4 Illustrator Large Canvas EPS samples as #2031 (environment, samples and layer inventory there). VectorCraft 0.10.0, Windows 11 x64, French UI.

**Severity:** Medium, to confirm

## Data
Sample D: 535.8 MB file. Its editing data is 295.4 MB of zstd that decodes to 2,043.6 MB (23.3 M lines), with 196 raster blocks. The PostScript part is 154 MB with 88 image operators.

VectorCraft has a hard limit ("it decompresses to more than …", "decoded data is too large"). We could not find the value and did not open sample D on screen.

## Expected
Stream the decode (ASCII85 > zstd > line parser) instead of buffering it whole. Make the limit configurable and show progress. If the limit is reached, still import the layer tree.

title: Window edge resize and title bar move work only every other time on Linux (X11): the window manager keeps the button release, egui keeps the drag

2. Drag the left window edge outwards and release: the window resizes.
3. Drag the same edge again: nothing happens.
4. Drag it a third time: the window resizes again.

A window move by the app bar blocks the next resize the same way. A click inside the window in between makes the next resize work.

| 6x the same 40 pt inwards (the pointer never leaves the window) | `EFEFEF` |
| 3x move the window by the app bar, then one zone drag | `FFF` |

```sh

title: Layers panel does not reveal the active layer after canvas selection
author: earlvanze
body:
When canvas selection changes to an object in a layer outside the visible part of a long Layers panel, the engine updates the active layer but the panel does not scroll to reveal it.

Current implementation auto-reveals newly highlighted Layers-panel rows, but a canvas selection does not add a highlighted row, so that reveal path is skipped.

Expected: after selecting art on the canvas, make its containing active layer visible in the Layers panel without disrupting a deliberate panel selection.

Reported in the VectorCraft Discord by @pavelzuk on 2026-10-14.

title: Actions: assign keyboard shortcuts, including alignment actions
author: earlvanze
body:
Request: allow a recorded Action to be assigned a keyboard shortcut, including actions containing alignment commands; ideally expose individual alignment commands for direct shortcut assignment.

Source: https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557517495470915686/1560104474700152954

Current checkout: crates/ui-egui/src/panels/actions.rs stores Action name and steps, with panel playback; no per-action shortcut field. Existing #1629 concerns editing/deleting actions, and open #1938 concerns batch processing, so neither tracks this specific request. General keyboard-shortcut support exists, but does not establish parameterized alignment/action shortcut coverage.

Acceptance: assign and persist a shortcut per action, handle conflicts, avoid triggering during text entry, and execute the same undoable action as panel playback. Assess direct alignment shortcut entries separately.

title: Window falls back to llvmpipe on Raspberry Pi 5 (V3D 7.1): wgpu device limits exceed the adapter's
author: nictoumayan
body:
VectorCraft 0.11.0 (arm64 .deb) opens on this machine, but only on the llvmpipe software rasterizer. Its window can't create a device on either of the GPU's real adapters.

**Machine:** Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 Lite (BCM2712, V3D 7.1.10.2), Debian 13 (trixie), Mesa 26.2.2 (`26.2.2-1~bpo13+0~rpt1`), labwc on Wayland.

```
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Limit 'max_inter_stage_shader_variables' value 16 is better than allowed 15
ERROR [main] vectorcraft::gpu: the window failed on graphics adapter Vulkan:14e4:55701c33 (WGPU error: Limit 'max_inter_stage_shader_variables' value 16 is better than allowed 15): starting again without it
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Limit 'max_texture_dimension_2d' value 8192 is better than allowed 4096
ERROR [main] vectorcraft::gpu: the window failed on graphics adapter Gl:14e4:0000 (WGPU error: Limit 'max_texture_dimension_2d' value 8192 is better than allowed 4096): starting again without it
WARN  [main] egui_wgpu: Software rasterizer detected - loss of performance expected. backend: Vulkan, device_type: Cpu, name: "llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 128 bits)", ...
```

**Cause:** eframe 0.36's default `WgpuSetupCreateNew::device_descriptor` (egui-wgpu 0.36.2) requests `wgpu::Limits::default()` on every backend except GL, and `downlevel_webgl2_defaults()` on GL, in both cases with `max_texture_dimension_2d: 8192`. It never checks what the adapter offers, so `request_device` fails when the adapter falls short on any single limit. V3D 7.1 falls short on several:

|---|---|---|---|
| `max_inter_stage_shader_variables` | 16 | 15 (`maxVertexOutputComponents` = 64) | |
| `max_texture_dimension_2d` | 8192 | 7680 | 4096 |

wgpu stops at the first failing limit, so the error only names one of them. egui's own shaders need far less than any of these.

**Fix:** wrap the default descriptor and lower each requested l…

title: vectorcraft --help opens the app instead of printing usage
author: switch87
body:
## What happens

The desktop binary treats `--help` (and `-h`) as a file to open and starts the app. Run from a terminal, SSH session or an agent's shell, it then never returns: the window opens (or, with no display, the start fails with a winit error) and nothing tells you about `vectorcraft-cli`.

```sh
$ vectorcraft --version
vectorcraft 0.10.0            # fine, exits before any window
$ vectorcraft --help          # opens the app (headless: hangs until killed)
$ env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY vectorcraft --help
… ERROR [main] vectorcraft: VectorCraft stopped: winit EventLoopError: … neither WAYLAND_DISPLAY nor WAYLAND_SOCKET nor DISPLAY is set.
```

I ran into this while scripting a design headless (`vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless`): `vectorcraft --help` was the first thing tried to find the options, and the process hung.

## Expected

`vectorcraft --help` / `-h` prints the desktop app's usage (`--control`, `--automation-read-root`, `--automation-write-root`, `--in-window-menus`, files) and exits 0 before logging, preferences or the window are set up, like `--version` already does. The text points to `vectorcraft-cli` for headless work (convert, run, MCP).

I'm working on this.

title: MCP draw_path / draw_shape: optional opacity, name, dash, cap and effects
author: switch87
body:
## Problem

`draw_path` and `draw_shape` (MCP) take the geometry plus `fill`, `stroke` and `strokeWidth` (and `fill`/`stroke` already accept a full gradient object, which is great). Everything else an object usually needs right after it is drawn costs one extra call each:

| want | today |
|---|---|
| a name for the Layers panel | `object.setProps {ids:[id], name}` |
| opacity | `object.setProps {ids:[id], opacity}` |
| a dashed seam / zipper line | `stroke.set {ids:[id], dash:[4,3], cap:"round"}` |
| a soft shadow | `effect.apply {ids:[id], effect:"blur.gaussian", params:{radius}}` |

A real example: I drew a set of cycling jerseys headless (`vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless`), hundreds of paths. The helper every path went through ended up as:

```python
i = v.tool('draw_path', d=d, fill=fill, stroke=stroke, strokeWidth=sw)['id']
v.cmd('object.setProps', ids=[i], opacity=opacity)
v.cmd('effect.apply', ids=[i], effect='blur.gaussian', params={'radius': blur})
v.cmd('object.setProps', ids=[i], name=name)
```

A dashed stitch line is `draw_path` → `stroke.set {dash}`, a blurred shadow 3 to 4 round trips. Over MCP every round trip counts.

## Proposal

Optional arguments on `draw_path` and `draw_shape`, applied to the new object in the same call:

```json
{"d": "M230 300 L230 900", "stroke": "#c19a4b", "strokeWidth": 1.2,
 "dash": [4, 3], "cap": "round", "join": "round",
 "opacity": 60, "name": "Zip seam",
 "effects": [{"effect": "blur.gaussian", "params": {"radius": 6}}]}
```

- `opacity` 0..100 and `name` as `object.setProps` takes them;
- `dash` (lengths, or null), `cap`, `join` as `stroke.set` takes them, sent in the same `stroke.set` as `strokeWidth`;
- `effects`: a list of `{effect, params?}` applied in order, as `effect.apply` / `apply_effect`.

Values are checked before anything is drawn, so a typo doesn't leave a half-styled object behind.

I'm working on this.

title: MCP command_batch: allow draw_path and draw_shape as steps, returning the new ids
author: switch87
body:
## Problem

`command_batch` is the way to cut MCP round trips, but its steps are engine commands only. The two tools agents draw with most, `draw_path` and `draw_shape`, are MCP tools, so they can't be a step:

```json
{"steps": [{"id": "draw_path", "params": {"d": "M0 0 L100 0 L50 80 Z", "fill": "#550505", "stroke": "none"}}]}
→ step 0: unknown command `draw_path`
```

The engine commands underneath (`path.create`, `shape.rectangle`, …) can be batched, but then every object needs its paint as separate steps (`paint.setFill {ids:"$0.id"}`, `paint.setStroke`, `stroke.set`), which is exactly what `draw_path` saves you.

Real case: a full cut pattern for a cycling jersey (7 pieces, a few hundred facet paths, clipping, transforms and text), drawn with `vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless`, took several minutes, mostly in per-call round trips, because each `draw_path` had to be its own `tools/call`.

## Proposal

`draw_path` and `draw_shape` are accepted as step ids in `command_batch`, with the same arguments as the tools (and the same unknown-argument check). The step's result is the tool's result, so the new object's id is in `results[N].result.id` and later steps can refer to it:

```json
{"atomic": true, "label": "Facets", "steps": [
  {"id": "draw_path", "params": {"d": "M0 0 L100 0 L50 80 Z", "fill": "#550505", "stroke": "none"}},
  {"id": "draw_shape", "params": {"shape": "rectangle", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 100, "height": 80, "fill": "#000000"}},
  {"id": "object.setProps", "params": {"id": "$0.id", "name": "Facet 1"}}
]}
```

The reply also lists the ids made by the drawing steps (`created`), so a caller doesn't have to dig them out of each result.

I'm working on this.

title: paint.setFill: one gradient across several objects (span: "selection")
author: switch87
body:
## Problem

A gradient given to several objects is fitted to **each object's own box**: `paint.setFill {ids:[…], gradient:{…}}` on 300 triangles gives 300 small, identical ramps, not one ramp running across the set. With the Gradient tool you can drag one vector across several selected objects so they share a single gradient (Illustrator's public help describes the same for its Gradient tool: https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/gradients.html). There is no command form of that.

Today the only way is to work out the union of the objects' bounds yourself and pass the vector in document coordinates (`gradient.start` / `gradient.end`), which is easy to get wrong for an angle or a radial gradient.

Real case: a low-poly (faceted) cycling jersey drawn headless with `vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless`. Every facet's colour had to be computed in the script, by sampling the ramp at the triangle's centroid:

![Faceted jersey: every triangle's colour sampled from one vertical ramp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/vectorcraft-gradient-span-facets.jpg)

With one gradient over the whole set, the ramp could be applied once and the facets would only add their tint jitter.

## Proposal

An optional `span` on `paint.setFill` and `paint.setStroke`:

```json
{"command": "paint.setFill", "params": {
  "ids": [12, 13, 14, …],
  "gradient": {"kind": "linear", "angle": -90,
               "stops": [{"offset": 0, "color": "#f7f0e3"}, {"offset": 0.5, "color": "#c19a4b"}, {"offset": 1, "color": "#550505"}]},
  "span": "selection"}}
```

- `span: "object"` (default): what happens now, each object fits the gradient to its own bounds.
- `span: "selection"`: the gradient is placed once on the union of the targets' bounds (the `ids`, else the selection) at its `angle` (and `aspect` for radial) and every target gets that same vector in document coordinates, so the ramp runs continuously across them, as a Gradient-tool drag across the selection wou…

title: Selection-only commands (object.group, clippingMask.make, arrange, …) take optional ids
author: switch87
body:
## Problem

Many object commands work only on the selection and take no `ids`, so a script has to send `select.set {ids}` first, one extra round trip per call, and the result depends on whatever is selected at that moment. Commands like `paint.setFill`, `object.setProps`, `object.transform` and (since 0.10.0) `stroke.set` already take `ids?|id?`, and since #1577 a command that documents `ids` is enabled as it is with them selected.

Real case: a headless jersey design (`vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless`) with many groups and clip groups. The helpers ended up as:

```python
def group(ids, name):
    v.cmd('select.set', ids=ids)
    g = v.cmd('object.group')['id']
    v.cmd('object.setProps', ids=[g], name=name)

def clip(ids, clip_d, name):
    c = shape(clip_d, fill='#000000')
    v.cmd('select.set', ids=ids + [c])
    r = v.cmd('object.clippingMask.make')
    …
```

Selection-only commands an agent typically needs, with no `ids` on `main` today:

- `object.group`, `object.ungroup`
- `object.clippingMask.make`, `object.clippingMask.release`
- `object.compoundPath.make`, `object.compoundPath.release`
- `object.arrange.bringToFront` / `bringForward` / `sendBackward` / `sendToBack` / `sendToCurrentLayer`
- `object.lock`, `object.hide`
- `edit.duplicate`
- `object.move`, `object.rotate`, `object.scale`, `object.reflect`, `object.shear`
- the ten `object.pathfinder.*` commands

## Proposal

These commands take an optional `ids?|id?`, as `object.setProps` does: the objects given are selected first (as `select.set` selects them, with its validation) and the command then runs on them as it does on the selection, in the same undo step. The result and the selection afterwards are what the menu command gives (`object.group {ids:[3,4]}` → `{id}` of the new group, selected). Without `ids` nothing changes.

```json
{"command": "object.group", "params": {"ids": [3, 4]}}
{"command": "object.clippingMask.make", "params": {"ids": [7, 8, 9, 12]}}
```

I'm working on this.

title: CI: make the PR gate match cargo xtask ci (local-first)
author: Messhias
body:
## Context

CI is the biggest bottleneck right now. Most PRs that only touch Rust sources never run a full workspace gate on GitHub. FreeBSD is the only job that runs `cargo test --workspace`, and on pull requests it is limited to Cargo.toml / packaging / workflow paths. Typical PRs get Affinity corpus only, or nothing. Forks often sit in `action_required` until a maintainer approves workflows by hand. There is no macOS test job, so platform float issues (see #1770) show up only on contributor machines. The release pipeline itself is fine; the problem is PR throughput and coverage.

The local quality gate is already `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, assets, brands, layers, wasm). GitHub does not run that on ordinary code PRs.

## Goal

Every code PR gets the same gate people run locally, without making FreeBSD the daily gate (it is expensive). Maintainers spend less time approving and re-running Actions. Merges to main require that gate.

## Proposal

### Phase 1 (P0)

1. Add an Ubuntu job on every PR (and push to main) that touches `crates/**`, `apps/**`, `xtask/**`, or workspace Cargo files. The job runs `cargo xtask ci` (same steps as local). Use cache and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` so minutes stay reasonable.
2. Make that job the required status check for main.
3. Keep FreeBSD on push to main and on packaging / dependency path changes. Do not use it as the per-PR gate for ordinary crate edits.
4. Reduce the fork approval queue: mark recurring contributors as trusted where the org allows it, and document in CONTRIBUTING that a first-time fork PR needs "Approve and run workflows".

### Phase 2 (P1)

5. Close the macOS gap for float-sensitive tests (#1770): either a small macOS job for those targets, or make the pinned tests tolerate last-bit differences and keep a light smoke on release if needed.
6. Affinity corpus stays as today when its paths change.

### Phase 3 (P2)

7. Centralizing workflows via craft-common-actions (#1184) is fine after Phas…

97% of the page height (the rest is the marks margin) and flat colours are identical in …

title: The built-in "High Quality Print" preset ignores the document bleed
author: IncusAudio
body:
**Environment:** VectorCraft 0.10.0 (`vectorcraft-cli --version`), release build from source, commit `0d0ea352` (`v0.10.0-310-g0d0ea352`), driven through the headless MCP engine. macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), arm64, Apple M1 Pro. **Why an AI assistant was involved:** the reporter hit print-export problems in VectorCraft and asked an AI assistant (Claude Code), using VectorCraft's own CLI and MCP server, to diagnose them. This report was drafted by that assistant from measurements taken during the session. The reporter said the export was missing bleed, especially on the left of page 1, when using the High Quality Print preset. The cause was this preset.

---

**Severity:** medium (silent: no warning, file just has no bleed).

`crates/pdf/src/presets.rs`: `print(ImageCodec::Auto, false)` sets `bleed.use_document = false`, so a
document with 3 mm bleed exports with MediaBox = TrimBox = BleedBox. *Press Quality* and the PDF/X
presets use the document bleed. A user picking "High Quality Print" for a print job gets no bleed and no
indication. Suggest defaulting `use_document` to true for that preset, or warning when the document has
a non-zero bleed and the preset ignores it.

author: IncusAudio
body:

title: Plug-in API v2: requirements from a suite of 18 Illustrator panels
author: nelio7
body:
Following up on #710. I'd like to add a concrete use case for plug-in API v2 (gap G17). It overlaps with the PhotoCraft proposals in storytold/photocraft#662 and storytold/photocraft#4301.

I maintain a suite of about 18 Illustrator CEP panels for urban planning, used by a small group. They:
- import official open geodata into to-scale drawings (OSM/Overpass; OGC API and WMS services from NRW, Brandenburg and Wallonia; terrain tiles)
- extrude building footprints into axonometric views with pitched roofs and shadows
- draw sections and street cross-sections, measurements and scale bars
- include pattern and recolour tools and a library panel
- come with a manager that installs and updates the panels from a shared folder

I'd love to move them to VectorCraft. Here is everything they rely on, so v2 could cover a suite like this completely.

**Must-have**

title: PDF export: oversized Form BBoxes and off-page sentinel clips may prevent moving artwork in Illustrator
author: ludovic-coder
body:
## Summary
Two VectorCraft exports used for print production opened in Illustrator but could not be moved. Inspection found extremely large Form XObject bounds and small, non-painting clipping paths far outside the page. An external cleanup was followed by a successful manipulation test by a colleague.

This report contains technical observations only. Client artwork, screenshots of artwork, filenames and embedded editing payloads are intentionally not attached.

## Environment and scope
- VectorCraft on macOS.
- Original embedded editing payloads identified generators 0.4.0 and 0.10.0. The exact build used for subsequent exports was not recorded.
- The currently installed macOS app reports 0.11.0; this does NOT establish that the problem has been reproduced on 0.11.0.
- The print provider reports using Illustrator 2026; the exact Illustrator patch/build and OS were not supplied. The colleague's exact build for the earlier move test is unknown.
- Both PDF and PDF-backed .ai files were involved. Layer-enabled PDF reexports also contained the structures below.

## Actual behavior
Illustrator displayed this French error when attempting to move artwork:
> Impossible de déplacer les objets. La transformation requise rendrait certains objets trop grands.

Translation: Cannot move the objects; the requested transformation would make some objects too large.

## Observed PDF structure
Several Form XObjects had:

```text
/BBox [-32767 -32767 32767 32767]
```

That is approximately 23 metres across in default PDF units, despite an ordinary-sized page.

Their content included standalone sequences such as:

```text
q
-32000 0 m
-31999 0 l
-31999 1 l
h
W
n
Q
```

Other sequences used x = -32001/-32000 or small y offsets. These clips were established and then immediately discarded by Q without painting anything.

In two inspected exports, the cleanup removed 48 and 7 such sequences respectively, and corrected seven oversized BBoxes in each file.

title: Plug-in API v2: panel plug-ins with form controls and a drawing surface
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (see also #121 and storytold/photocraft#662).

**Need:** a `panel` plug-in kind: a dockable panel that follows the app theme and offers
- declarative form controls (numbers, sliders, checkboxes, dropdowns, buttons, lists), and
- a drawing surface the plug-in paints itself (vector shapes, text, raster images), with pointer and wheel events.

**Use case:** my panels show live preview sketches that redraw as settings change (extrusion direction and roof shape, shadow angle, street cross-section). The geodata panel shows a pannable, zoomable map built from raster tiles.

title: Plug-in API v2: document access at the level of the command registry
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (see also #121).

**Need:** plug-ins can read the selection and the whole document (layers, groups, objects with geometry and paint, artboards, swatches). They can also run commands at the level of the command registry: create and edit paths, compound paths, groups, layers (order, lock, visibility), artboards, new documents, global/spot swatches, type, placed or embedded images, clipping masks, symbols and Pathfinder operations. Everything one plug-in action changes is one undo step. Today's object filters only see selected paths and can only return paths.

**Use case:** a geodata import creates layers, spot swatches, thousands of paths, labels and embedded map images. The extrusion and section tools build grouped scenes on their own layers and new artboards.

title: Per-object metadata: notes and namespaced key/value data readable by plug-ins
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179.

**Need:** plug-ins can read and write an object's note and namespaced key/value data (like Illustrator's tags). The data is saved in the native file, kept through duplicate, copy/paste and grouping, and readable by other plug-ins.

**Use case:** the geodata panel stores building height, storeys and roof shape on each footprint, and the extrusion panel reads them later. Shadows keep a reference to their building so they can be rebuilt after it moves.

title: Plug-in events: selection, document and object changes
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179.

**Need:** panel plug-ins can subscribe to these events: selection changed, document activated/opened/closed, objects changed (moved, transformed, deleted) and theme changed.

**Use case:** panels refresh their counts and previews when the selection changes. Derived art (ground shadows, the drawing order of extruded buildings) is updated when buildings move.

title: Plug-in commands with menu entries and assignable shortcuts
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (see also the `command` kind in storytold/photocraft#662).

**Need:** plug-ins register actions as real commands, available in a menu, the command palette, Actions, MCP and Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts.

**Use case:** "Extrude selection" on a shortcut without opening the panel. In Illustrator this needs a separate macOS hotkey helper app.

title: Plug-in network access beyond loopback (HTTPS to declared hosts, approved by the user)
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (related: storytold/photocraft#4301, which proposes loopback only).

**Need:** a capability for HTTPS requests to the hosts a plug-in's manifest declares, approved by the user per plug-in and revocable, alongside loopback.

**Use case:** the geodata panel loads public open data: OSM via Overpass and Nominatim, OGC API Features and WMS services of NRW, Brandenburg and Wallonia, and terrain tiles. A loopback-only rule would force a separate local proxy process.

title: Plug-in storage: settings, a cache, and files picked through host dialogs
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179.

**Need:** per-plug-in persistent settings, a cache with a sizeable quota (hundreds of MB) that the user can clear, and access to files and folders the user picks in the host's open/save dialogs.

**Use case:** cached map tiles and geodata, a library panel that reads a user-chosen library folder, and tools that export files.

title: Plug-in long-running jobs: progress, cancel and larger limits
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179.

**Need:** progress reporting and cancel for plug-in runs, and limits that allow tens of thousands of objects and several minutes per run (v1: 60 s per filter run, at most 100,000 output objects).

**Use case:** importing a district with up to 50,000 geodata objects, or extruding 1,000+ buildings with roofs and shadows.

title: JavaScript plug-ins on the scripting runtime
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (related: #1161, #1183).

**Need:** plug-ins written in JavaScript that run on the Boa runtime from #1183, with the same manifest, sandbox and capabilities as WASM plug-ins.

**Use case:** CEP and UXP panels are written in JavaScript. Existing logic, such as several thousand lines of roof-skeleton and drawing-order code, could be reused instead of rewritten in Rust.

title: ExtendScript compatibility for the Illustrator scripting DOM
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179 (precedent: EffectCraft already runs `.jsx` scripts and ScriptUI panels).

**Need:** run `.jsx` scripts against a compatible subset of Illustrator's documented scripting DOM, built from Adobe's public scripting reference: `app.activeDocument`, `documents`, `layers`, `pathItems`, `compoundPathItems`, `groupItems`, `textFrames`, `placedItems`, `swatches`/`spots`, `artboards`, `selection`, `note`, `tags`, `zOrder`, `duplicate`.

**Use case:** the host-side code of existing Illustrator panels and scripts could run mostly unchanged, which would make moving a whole suite realistic.

title: Plug-in distribution: install and update from a catalog
author: nelio7
body:
Part of #2179.

**Need:** install and update plug-ins from a file, a folder or a URL catalog, with versions, update checks and signatures.

**Use case:** a small team gets panel updates from a shared folder. Today a custom manager panel installs and updates them.
