title: Selection tool: respect rotated canvas view
author: earlvanze
body:
## Request

When the canvas view is rotated, the Selection tool should keep its hit-testing, bounding box, handles, and drag transforms aligned with the rotated artboard and artwork.

## Context

A community illustrator requested that selection respect artboard rotation while drawing on a rotated canvas view. VectorCraft already has Rotate View support, but this exact Selection-tool behavior is not currently documented or covered by an open issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- Clicking and marquee-selecting use the rotated canvas transform.
- Selection outlines, bounding boxes, and handles remain aligned with the rotated artwork.
- Moving, scaling, and rotating selected objects work correctly at non-zero view rotations.
- Automated coverage exercises at least one rotated-view Selection workflow.

title: SVG export writes unitless width/height for a millimetre document, so it renders at 75 % of its size
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** A document in millimetres is exported to SVG with `width`/`height` in user units (CSS px) holding the point values. A 50 × 30 mm drawing comes out as `width="141.732" height="85.039"`, which browsers and other SVG tools read as 141.732 px = 37.5 mm. Opening a `width="50mm"` SVG and saving it again loses its physical size the same way.

**Environment.** vectorcraft-cli 0.13.1 (macOS universal, headless), macOS 26, Apple M4 Max.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```sh
cat > mm.svg <<'EOF'
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="50mm" height="30mm" viewBox="0 0 50 30">
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="40" height="20" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1"/>
</svg>
EOF
vectorcraft-cli info mm.svg            # "units": "Millimeters", artboard 141.73 × 85.04 pt (= 50 × 30 mm, read correctly)
vectorcraft-cli convert mm.svg out.svg
head -2 out.svg

# Same with a new document:
vectorcraft-cli run --cmd file.new --params '{"width":"50 mm","height":"30 mm","units":"Millimeters"}' \
  --cmd shape.rectangle --params '{"x":14.17,"y":14.17,"width":113.39,"height":56.69}' --export new.svg
head -2 new.svg
```

**Actual.** Both files: `<svg … width="141.732" height="85.039" viewBox="0 0 141.732 85.039">`, no unit. At 96 px/in that is 37.5 × 22.5 mm. I found no SVG export option to choose the unit (`responsive` drops width/height altogether).

**Expected.** The size keeps its physical value, e.g. `width="50mm" height="30mm"` for a millimetre document (the viewBox can stay in points), or at least `width="141.732pt"`. An option for the unit would be fine too, if px has to stay the default.

**Why / use case.** Technical diagrams and logos for print and for CAD/office tools, where 1:1 size matters. An agent that exports a 50 mm logo gets a 37.5 mm one with no warning.

title: [Bug] .ai import: Clip Group renders background polygon on top of underlying paths, obscuring contents (v0.13.1)
author: QianyeSu
body:
### Summary
When importing an Adobe Illustrator (`.ai`) file containing a Clipping Group (`Clip Group`), VectorCraft renders the contents strictly in sequential stream order. If Illustrator's PDF-compatible stream placed the base background/clipping polygon at the end of the group, VectorCraft renders this opaque polygon over all preceding clipped paths, completely obscuring them.

The exact same file renders correctly in Adobe Illustrator because Illustrator uses its internal `AIPrivateData` object tree where the background/mask sits underneath the clipped artwork.

### Environment
- **VectorCraft Version**: 0.13.1 (macOS Universal)
- **VectorCraft CLI**: 0.13.1
- **OS**: macOS

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In Adobe Illustrator, create a 3D isometric map scene with a clipping group:
   - Group contains ~20 continent vector paths (`#f6f4e7`) on a surface plane.
   - A full-surface ocean polygon (`#c0e1e8`) covers the entire clipped bounding box (`M446.944 132.727 L195.755 262.437 L94.69 209.095 L350.806 81.061 Z`).
2. Save as standard Illustrator `.ai` (PDF-compatible).
3. Open the `.ai` file in Adobe Illustrator:
   - Continents are clearly visible sitting on top of the blue ocean.
4. Open the exact same `.ai` file in VectorCraft (or convert via `vectorcraft-cli`):
   - The entire surface appears solid cyan/blue; all continent paths underneath are completely obscured.

### Technical Analysis & Root Cause
Inspecting the imported SVG/DOM structure via `vectorcraft-cli convert` reveals:
```xml
<g id="ClipGroup" clip-path="url(#clip-path-2)">
  <!-- Child 0..19: Continents -->
  <path fill="#f6f4e7" stroke="#a9b3b5" ... />
  ...
  <!-- Child 20: Full-bounding ocean polygon placed at the END of the group -->
  <g clip-path="url(#clip-path-3)">
    <path d="M446.944 132.727 L195.755 262.437 L94.69 209.095 L350.806 81.061 Z" fill="#c0e1e8" />
  </g>
</g>
```

Because VectorCraft follows strict painter's algorithm order (bottom-to-top) from the stream, `Child 20` is drawn las…

title: [Feature Request] File Sharing and Real-Time Collaboration in VectorCraft over Local Network or Online
author: MarkShand
body: Dear VectorCraft Team, I would like to request a file-sharing and collaboration feature similar to Figcraft, as shown in the attached screenshot. It would be helpful if users could: - **Share files online** using an invite link or join code. - **Collaborate over a local network**, with files staying within the network without passing through an external server. - **Edit the same design together in real time**, with changes visible to everyone. - **See collaborators’ names, cursors, and selections** to help coordinate work. - **Set access permissions**, such as view-only or editing access. - **Leave comments and feedback** directly on the design. A simple **Share** button with options to start a session or join using a code or invite link would make collaboration easier. This would help teams review designs, make changes together, and avoid exchanging multiple versions of the same file. Thank you for considering this feature request.

title: [Feature Request] Support saving / exporting to CorelDRAW (.cdr) format
author: luoyunxiaotian
body:
### Problem Statement / Motivation
CorelDRAW (`.cdr`) is one of the most widely used vector graphics formats in the advertising, print shop, laser cutting/engraving, sign making, and CNC manufacturing industries, particularly across China, East Asia, and parts of Europe and Latin America.

Currently, VectorCraft provides great support for vector formats like `.svg`, `.pdf`, `.ai`, `.dxf`, and `.eps`. However, many production vendors and print shops strictly request native `.cdr` files from designers. As a result, users currently have to perform an extra conversion step (e.g. exporting to PDF/SVG/EPS and re-saving in CorelDRAW or third-party software), which creates workflow friction and risks potential formatting/attribute losses.

---

### Proposed Feature
Add export / "Save As" support for CorelDRAW (`.cdr`) format in both the GUI and CLI:
- **GUI:** Available in `File > Export` / `Save As` format selection.
- **CLI:** Supported in `vectorcraft-cli convert input.vectorcraft output.cdr` (and batch export channels).

---

### Technical Context & Implementation Considerations
1. **Modern CDR Format Structure (X4+):**
   - From CorelDRAW X4 onwards, `.cdr` files are standard **PKZIP archives** containing XML files and media (e.g., `content/riffData.cdr`, `content/root.xml`, document metadata, and embedded color/media streams).
   - This makes modern CDR generation much more approachable than legacy proprietary binary blobs, as basic geometry, fills, strokes, and text can be serialized to XML/ZIP.
2. **Prior Art & Open Source Reference:**
   - The [Document Liberation Project / `libcdr`](https://www.documentliberation.org/projects/libcdr/) provides extensive documentation and reverse-engineered specifications on CDR structures.
   - The [sK1 Project / UniConvertor](https://sk1project.net/) also features documented implementations for parsing and generating CorelDRAW-compatible vector data.
3. **Alternative / Incremental Step:**
   - If full native `.cdr` writing requir…

title: Add support for Android Vector Drawable (XML) import and export
author: sakata2009
body:
### Description
I would like to suggest adding support for **Android Vector Drawable (XML)**, the vector graphics format natively used in **Android Studio** for Android applications. 

Ideally, this should include two capabilities:
1. **Export:** The ability to export vector paths directly into an Android-compatible XML file (utilizing tags like `<vector>`, `<group>`, and `<path>` with attributes like `android:pathData`, `android:fillColor`, etc.).
2. **Import:** The ability to open or drag-and-drop an Android vector XML file directly onto the canvas to edit its paths.

### Use Case / Problem
Currently, UI/UX designers creating assets for Android apps have to export drawings as SVG and then use external converters or the "Vector Asset Studio" inside Android Studio to transform them into Android XML format. 

Having native XML Vector support in VectorCraft would eliminate these intermediate steps, making it an incredibly powerful tool for mobile developers and designers who want to streamline their asset pipeline.

### Additional Context
Android Vector Drawables are subset-based XML variations closely related to SVGs, but they map paths using standard syntax (e.g., `M15,4H14...`) inside custom Android XML schemas. 
More details about the format can be found in the [Android Developer Documentation](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/graphics/vector-drawable-resources).

title: `vectorcraft-cli run`: read the commands from a file (Windows limits a command line to 32,767 characters)
author: pandapknaepel
body:
## Summary

`vectorcraft-cli run` takes every command as `--cmd ID --params JSON` on the command line. On Windows a process command
line is limited to 32,767 characters (`CreateProcess`), so a batch run fails as soon as its parameters get long – e.g.
`file.place` with `dataBase64` (a small SVG barcode is already several KB), a few hundred `paint.setFill`/`object.setProps`
calls with id lists, or `path.create` with many anchors. On Linux/macOS the same run works.

Splitting a run is not equivalent: commands later in a run often refer to ids created earlier in it, and new ids are only
predictable inside one run.

## Wanted

One of:

```sh
vectorcraft-cli run --in doc.vectorcraft --commands steps.json --export out.pdf
# steps.json: [{"command":"file.place","params":{…}}, {"command":"object.setProps","params":{…}}, …]
```

or `--params @file.json` (read one command's parameters from a file), or the commands as JSON lines on stdin
(`--commands -`). The output could stay as it is (one JSON result line per step).

## Example (today, Windows)

```sh
vectorcraft-cli run --in sheet.vectorcraft ^
  --cmd file.place --params "{\"name\":\"code.svg\",\"dataBase64\":\"<40 KB>\",\"rect\":[20,40,16,57]}" ^
  --cmd object.setProps --params "{\"name\":\"barcode\"}"
```

→ the process cannot be started (command line too long); the same arguments run on Linux.

VectorCraft 0.13.1, Windows 10/11 (limit), checked on Linux x86-64 that `run` has no file/stdin option.

title: Support importing HPG / HPGL files from garment CAD software
author: paolobrunello92-cpu
body:
We would like to request support for opening/importing .HPG (HPGL) files in VectorCraft.

We work in clothing production and use files generated by garment CAD software. Currently, we use CorelDRAW almost exclusively to open these files. Supporting this format would help us move this workflow to VectorCraft.

Expected behavior:

* Import the outlines as editable vector paths.
* Preserve the original physical dimensions and scale, with measurements available in millimeters.
* Preserve the arrangement of the pattern pieces and their text labels.

Our sample file, “Giubbino corto.HPG”, contains text-based HPGL commands, including IN, CS, IW, SP, PU, PD, ES, SI, DI, LB and PG. Its header indicates 100% scale on both axes.

We can provide this sample file and a screenshot of how it appears in CorelDRAW to help with implementation and testing.

Thank you!

[Giubbino corto.HPG.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33683272/Giubbino.corto.HPG.zip)

title: Print Dialog Issues
author: ryanghowell
body:
When printing from VectorCraft, the selected printer is not saved when clicking "done" on the print dialog.

Additionally, custom media sizes created in the Printer's config are not displaying in the VectorCraft media size dropdown.
